posts.caption: In 2021, one engineer typed one wrong command and 3.5 billion people lost the internet in a single instant. Not hacked. Not attacked. Just one wrong line of code during a routine maintenance check. Facebook's own engineers couldn't even log in to fix it, their access tools were on the same servers that just vanished. They had to physically drive to data centers and override servers by hand. One by one. 6 hours. $60 million lost every single hour. And the exact same vulnerability? Still exists right now. The internet is more fragile than you think.

2021 mein ek engineer ne ek galat command type ki aur 3.5 billion logon ka internet ek pal mein band ho gaya. Hack nahi hua. Attack nahi hua. Bas ek routine maintenance check ke dauran ek galat line of code. 6 ghante. Har ghante 60 million dollar ka nuksaan. Internet utna strong nahi jitna hum sochte hain.

There is a sound that only 2% of people can hear. Scientists have studied it for 50 years and still have no answer. It's called The Hum — and the leading theory is that it's the Earth itself vibrating at a frequency most humans aren't built to detect. A woman heard it for 11 years, moved across the country to escape it, and it followed her to the new house. Stop right now, close your eyes, and listen. What do you hear?

We call space the final frontier. But we've barely explored our own planet. Earth is stranger than anything we've found out there — and most people have no idea. From perfect solar eclipses to oceans deeper than mountains are tall, this is the planet you thought you knew.

In 1974, a man calculated the exact day he would die and spent a year preparing for it. What happened next is stranger than the prediction itself. Frank was obsessed with numerology. He told his family, quit his job, and gave away everything he owned. When the day came and went without incident, he thought he'd beaten fate. He hadn't.

After exploring most of Earth, venturing into space and exploring other planets, stars and galaxies seemed like an exciting, and even obvious next step. But the deeper we look, the more the universe reveals a hidden barrier between our Solar System and everything else around it. From the vast empty space, to the laws of physics themselves, there are many reasons why the dream of space travel might stay just a dream.

What is stopping us from reaching the stars? Why does space become more dangero

The second pin in our Cosmic Time Collection, celebrating phenomena that take place beyond our human timelines.

All the light in the Universe will eventually go extinct. How lucky you are to exist right now, in a brief and extraordinary moment in time when the Universe is still filled with stars and light, and when so much is still left to discover!

In Renaissance Europe, science was being transformed into a practice anyone could participate in and even enjoy. The field of astronomy grew rapidly as new instruments were crafted to make discoveries, as you can see on the August page of our 12,026 Human Era calendar. That is when champions like Tycho Brahe, an eccentric man with a metal nose, achieved notoriety by throwing astronomy parties and collecting great volumes of star data that we still use today.

Take a journey through the cosmos with us: Explore the vastness of our Solar System, the Milky Way, and beyond. From the Oort cloud to the Laniakea Supercluster, discover just how tiny we are in the grand scheme of the universe.

YouTube’s AI Detection Kicked Us in the Face

Every creator's worst nightmare just happened to us: The YouTube algorithm actually blocked us. It started slowly at first. Some videos started showing strange view fluctuations. Our second to last video did very badly, but this just happens sometimes, so we didn’t think that much about it. 

But then our last video, about Superpredators, did *extremely* badly. It was our worst upload since 2013. But it did badly in a weird way: Almost every single m

Your brain peaked at birth. Babies may seem helpless, but their brains are incredible learning machines. They can hear sounds from any language, recognize faces adults can't, and build millions of neural connections every second!

Someone should reach out to Barbie, we might have found the pinkest asteroid out there!

Are you ready for your space adventure? Star Birds, a game we developed together with our friends at @toukana_interactive, is available on Steam!
Moon dust is no joke: it floats, clings, and cuts like glass. Each landing sends deadly particles flying through space and scientists are still scrambling for fixes.
And here we thought spiders and insects are Australia's biggest threat... 😬

Back in 1932, Australia went to war against the most unusual enemy. It wasn't another country or an invading army. It was a flock of 20,000 emus! They invaded and devastated farmers' wheat fields and the government had no other option but to take out the big guns, literally. What followed has since become one of the strangest military operations in the history: the Great Emu War.

Watch our latest Nightshift video to find out what actually happened during the Emu War, how one of the world's larg
It seems that Midas have stumbled over a rock and fell on the ground. Surely nothing bad can come out of that... 👀

On the vast, cold seas with endless waves in all directions, there is one constant companion: the stars. Whenever they were visible, sailors knew they could find their way. Their guidance meant ships could dare to cross the oceans with nothing more than keen eyesight and the ability to read the signs in the sky. Just like the brave sailors aboard Chinese junks that can be seen on the July page of our 12,026 Human Era calendar, who left familiar shores to cross oceans and head into the unknown.

recentPosts.caption:
Neuschwanstein Castle looks like it came straight out of a storybook, but it was built as the personal retreat of King Ludwig II of Bavaria in the late 1800s.⁠
⁠
Its towers, mountain setting, and fairytale architecture later inspired Disney’s Sleeping Beauty Castle, turning it into one of the most recognizable castles in the world.⁠
⁠
Today, more than a million people visit every year to walk through its halls, admire the views over the Bavarian Alps, and see the castle that inspired generations

This is Ouzoud Falls 🌊🇲🇦⁠
⁠
Located in the Grand Atlas foothills near Tanaghmeft village, about 150km from Marrakech, these falls drop roughly 110 meters (360 ft) over multiple tiers into the El Abid River gorge. It’s also among the tallest waterfalls in North Africa.⁠
⁠
📷by: @moroccobyme

The Sedlec Ossuary, also known as the Bone Church, is decorated with the remains of thousands of people, with an estimated 40,000 to 70,000 skeletons used throughout the chapel.⁠
⁠
Inside, human bones were carefully arranged into works of art, such as chandeliers and crosses, by woodcarver František Rint.⁠
⁠
Today, it remains one of Czechia’s most fascinating landmarks, attracting visitors from around the world.⁠
⁠
Would you visit this unique church? ⁠
⁠
By: @visit.sedlec

Yehliu Geopark is famous for its hoodoo rocks, tall, narrow formations shaped over millions of years as wind, rain, sea spray, and waves slowly eroded the softer layers of stone.⁠
⁠
The park is home to dozens of rock formations named after what they resemble, but the most famous is the Queen's Head, a natural rock that looks like the profile of a queen.⁠
⁠
Have you ever heard of Yehliu Geopark?⁠
⁠
By: @vanandshan_ig  Alix Lee

In the middle of Serbia’s Drina River sits a tiny wooden house built on a single rock.⁠
⁠
The house near Bajina Bašta first appeared in 1968, when a group of young men built a small shelter where they could rest and enjoy the river during summer days. ⁠
⁠
Over the years, floods damaged the cabin several times, but it was rebuilt each time on the same piece of rock.⁠
⁠
By: vlailaa

Comment “HOTELS” and we’ll send you our list of 500 hotels that already work with creators 📩

Finding the right hotels is the easy part. Finding the person who actually approves collabs is what stops everyone.

500 hotels, direct contacts, all over the world, updated constantly.

Follow @travelcreator.club for the system behind it.

To discover a country is to explore its provinces too, and @withlaya showed us exactly why.⁠
⁠
Kanchanaburi, Thailand, is home to breathtaking landscapes, emerald rivers, lush mountains, and some of the country's most beautiful natural attractions.⁠
A reminder that some of the best travel experiences are found beyond the major cities.

With its bright red head and blue body, the red-headed rock agama looks like a tiny superhero from the African wilderness.⁠
⁠
These colorful lizards are especially known for the dramatic appearance of males, whose colors become more intense during breeding season. Their vivid shades help them attract mates and signal dominance among other males.⁠
⁠
They spend much of their time on rocky surfaces, where their strong limbs and sharp claws allow them to climb and move with ease.⁠
⁠
By: @hugo.sykes

@daysofahomebody captured the last generation of Haenyeo heading out to sea. 🌊⁠
This remarkable community of female free divers from South Korea's Jeju Island has spent generations harvesting seafood without oxygen tanks, relying only on skill, endurance, and knowledge passed down through the years.⁠
⁠
Today, most Haenyeo are elderly, making this centuries-old tradition a rare sight and an important part of Korea's cultural heritage.

This star-shaped village began as a military fortress in 1593, during the Dutch Revolt. Every point, wall, and canal had a purpose: to protect the only route connecting Germany with the Spanish-controlled city of Groningen. The pointed bastions gave soldiers a clear view of the surrounding land, while the moats made the fortress much harder to reach.⁠
⁠
Centuries later, the soldiers are gone, but the star remains. ⁠
⁠

Paying just $1 a year in rent sounds impossible, but it's real.⁠
⁠
In Augsburg, Germany, the Fuggerei has been offering affordable housing since 1521, making it the world's oldest social housing community still in operation.⁠
⁠
Residents still pay the original annual rent of just €0.88 (about $1), but there are a few conditions. Applicants must be Roman Catholic, live in Augsburg, demonstrate financial need, and pray daily for the founders.⁠
⁠

When a tree fell in the Amazon, its roots unearthed giant ceramic urns filled with ancient human remains. The vessels don't match any known ceramic tradition—leaving archaeologists unsure who buried them or how old they are. 

Discover more about this mystery at the link in bio. 

Photograph by Geórgea Holanda, Mamirauá Institute

A humpback cow and calf are joined by two males in the Cook Islands and photographed by @brianskerry. Males escort females with calves in hopes that they will be the next ones to mate with the mothers. Calves emit soft, whisper-like squeaks while adult males sing in low, guttural moans and high-pitched whoops and screeches.

See more incredible images from the National Geographic archive at the link in bio.

Research suggests mosquitoes can pick you out in a crowd using a variety of cues to home in on their targets. Odor distinguishes people from other animals, and some mosquitoes have evolved to seek out our unique bouquet.

Find out which scents they’re drawn to, what scientists recommend to keep them away—and how a future personalized repellant might work at the link in bio.

Micrograph By Dr. Tony Brain, Science Photo Library

Meet Kio, a little cub with a big destiny.

Follow his real life journey in #NatGeoLION, a new National Geographic documentary series from executive producers Jon Favreau and Mike Gunton. Trailer dropping Thursday Aug 6.

Photographer @remustiplea has spent years photographing tiny damselflies and has become deeply familiar with their behaviors. Here, one rests in a leaf hole in Romania. These insects are similar to dragonflies but have slimmer bodies and narrower wings.

See more Photos of the Day at the link in bio.

New drone footage from the Head of Bight, South Australia, shows a southern right whale mother resting belly-up, pectoral fins stretched into the air before slowly rotating to take a breath, then swiveling upside down again. They're the only large whale species documented doing this, but what's the purpose of this unusual behavior? Researchers now theorize it may be tied to energy conservation while nursing their calves, though there's another theory floating around.

Popping up for a breather, this hippo in the Lugenda River is one of many that call Mozambique’s Niassa National Reserve home. Photographer @ottowhitehead captured this footage while covering the reserve’s success in helping local people live alongside wild animals in one of Africa’s largest wildernesses, thanks to organizations like the @niassalionproject.

Few life forms on Earth will experience as many nights as a giant sequoia, which can live for 3,000 years. They're also the largest living thing by volume, with the famed General Sherman Tree in Sequoia National Park weighing roughly 1,400 tons.

Photograph by Keith Ladzinski (@ladzinski)

Twenty years ago, National Geographic Explorer and photographer @joelsartore began a crusade to document the complete spectrum of our planet’s animal kingdom. Today, his National Geographic Photo Ark project, supported by @natgeosociety, features more than 18,000 animals, including some of the most threatened species on Earth. During the 20-year project, some have disappeared, and others are rapidly slipping toward extinction.

Meet the Bartering Kings of Bali 👑
 
This unique stealing and bartering behaviour has been observed among Uluwatu’s macaques for more than 30 years. Younger monkeys learn it from older members of the group, allowing the tradition to be passed down through generations.

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

When the midnight cravings hit 🌙
 
As night falls across the Namib desert, a desert rain frog emerges from beneath the sand in search of food. With only a few hours before temperatures begin to rise, it must make the most of the cooler conditions to find enough food for itself.
 
Explore the world’s few remaining untouched landscapes with Eden: Untamed Planet. Find the full series via the link in our bio 🔗

#EdenUntamedPlanet #DesertRainFrog #NightHunt #Namib

One of the most extraordinary transformations in evolution 🦌🐋

Millions of years ago, some mammals returned to the water. And over generations they became more streamlined and limbs turned to flippers, making them aquatic marvels. 

Find out where to watch Evolution via the link in our bio 🔗💚

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

You are what you eat 🍽️

Roseate spoonbills have a diet that is thought to give them their pink plumage. Shrimps, crabs and crayfish contain organic pigments called carotenoids that changes their feather colour when eaten.

#EarthCapture by @batzellapaola

Didn’t see that coming 👀
 
Perfectly hidden beneath the mud and vegetation, a mugger crocodile waits as a thirsty chital deer approaches the water’s edge. In a split second, it launches from its hiding place, but will the deer manage to escape?

Nature never fails to surprise us 🌍

Discover 20 unforgettable Planet Earth moments that prove the natural world is stranger, smarter and more spectacular than we can ever imagine.

#PlanetEarth #ExtraordinaryAnimals #PE20

Is the anus an underrated innovation? 🍑

Mutations in an ancestor called the urbilaterian lengthened their bodies over generations. A tube formed with a mouth for eating and an anus for pooing. This was a breakthrough invention creating the one-way through-gut for continuous feeding.

#Evolution #ChrisPackham #Nature

A mouthful of teeth 🦁🦷

30 to be precise. As predators and carnivores, lions use their teeth to hunt and eat. They have twelve incisors, four canines, ten premolars and four molars for gripping prey and cutting meat.

Waiting for the perfect moment 🐆
 
Perched high above the ground, the leopard waits until an impala comes within striking distance. After staying completely still, it launches from the tree in one powerful leap, but will all that patience pay off?

How do you attract a female? 🦌🦕

The most attractive are usually the biggest and hairiest with prominent features. In reproduction, they pass their genes to the next generation, who inherit more exaggerated attributes. Over millions of years, animal traits modify for better mating chances.
